nodes.description: Most LESKRES missense and in-frame alleles (for example p.Leu192Pro, p.Ala367Pro, p.Thr357Met, p.Phe182del) produce a stably folded AGO2 that still binds and uses miRNA guides but has altered conformational dynamics around the L1 linker, helix-7 and PIWI loops. Kinetic, RNA Bind-n-Seq and knock-in mouse data led the authors to classify these alleles as gain of function, and they correlate with more severe clinical courses. The original 2020 cohort paper had described the tested alleles as loss of function, in the sense of excluding a dominant-negative effect; that earlier framing is recorded below as contrary evidence.

evidence.reference_title: Dysregulation of AGO2-miRNA dynamics underlies the AGO2-associated Lessel-Kreienkamp syndrome.
evidence.snippet: The combined results suggest patient mutations impact AGO2 targeting dynamics in a gain-of-function manner, leading to deregulation of the neuronal transcriptome and the observed neurodevelopmental anomalies.

nodes.description: A minority of LESKRES alleles abolish AGO2 function. The PIWI-domain missense p.Gly733Arg fails in almost every functional assay and does not bind target mRNAs, and a de novo 235.3-kb deletion removing the first three AGO2 exons (and part of PTK2) is predicted to cause haploinsufficiency. The mechanistic study associates this class with milder phenotypes than the gain-of-function class.

evidence.reference_title: Germline AGO2 mutations impair RNA interference and human neurological development.
evidence.snippet: Thus, mutations in AGO2 have two functional consequences: first, in the majority of the mutants, basic aspects of RISC formation and AGO2 function are not affected, and second the p.G733R mutant exhibits a loss-of-function in almost every assay, likely similar to the anticipated effect of the here identified 235.3-kb deletion.

evidence.reference_title: Germline AGO2 mutations impair RNA interference and human neurological development.
evidence.snippet: In addition, the de novo (as determined by qPCR analysis) long-range deletion affecting the first three AGO2 exons (Fig. 1b) is likely to result in haploinsufficiency (Supplementary Fig. 4), similar to deletions affecting both AGO1 and AGO314.

nodes.description: CRISPR knock-in mice carrying the mouse equivalent of the recurrent p.Leu192Pro allele. Heterozygotes are under-represented at birth and breed poorly, and their cortex shows transcriptome changes with over-repression of Ago2-bound mRNAs. Surviving animals appear healthy; no neurological or behavioural phenotype is reported. A knock-in line for the loss-of-function allele (human p.Gly733Arg) showed few transcriptome changes.

nodes.description: LESKRES variants change which miRNAs AGO2 carries, which strand of the miRNA duplex is retained as guide, and the abundance of 3'-modified isomiRs. Variants near the helix-7 hinge, especially p.Phe182del, cause the largest changes, which the authors interpret as impaired anchoring within the miRNA-binding pocket.

nodes.description: In cultured hippocampal neurons overexpressing p.Phe182del, p.Leu192Pro or p.Met364Thr AGO2, the density of AGO2-positive P-bodies in dendrites almost doubles, while somatic granules are unchanged. The authors infer impaired local dendritic translation and synaptic plasticity; this rests on overexpression in rodent neurons and has not been shown in patient neurons.

nodes.description: The convergent molecular consequence of both allele classes is abnormal miRNA-guided post-transcriptional silencing. Its direction is allele- and target-dependent: shRNA-reporter silencing was reduced for every single-residue allele in the 2020 cohort, yet among the later variants tested only p.Arg714Trp and p.Asn729His impaired that assay, and gain-of-function alleles over-repress endogenous targets.
